newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Imperial Bank Q2 profit rises.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Imperial Bank Q2 profit rises.

text.p: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce on Thursday capped off the second-quarter round of Canadian bank earnings with higher profits, but failed to deliver an expected dividend hike.

CIBC said its net income for the second quarter ended April 30 rose to C$370 million ($269.5 million) or C84 cents (61 cents) a share from C$339 million ($246.9 million) or C76 cents (55 cents) a share in the year-earlier quarter.

This year's second-quarter earnings included a net after-tax gain of C$50 million ($36.4 million) from a land sale, while last year's second-quarter earnings included an C$18 million ($13 million) gain.
CIBC, Canada's second biggest bank, added that its net strategic costs rose to C$68 million ($49.5 million) in the second quarter from a year earlier figure of C$52 million ($37.9 million).
The bank's earnings were higher than expectations, but disappointed investors had also expected a dividend hike.

Nesbitt Burns analyst Hugh Brown said Canadian banks were still poised for dividend increases in the second half, with perhaps some share splits among the higher priced stocks. CIBC split its stock 2-for-1 in March.

Midway through the fiscal year to end-October,, Canada's big six banks were on track for their fourth straight year of record earnings. Their 1996 collective earnings topped C$6 billion ($4.4 billion).
CIBC also announced on Thursday it planned to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
CIBC's shares fell C25 cents to C33.60 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday.
